title: Regularising contractual employees - the legal hurdles explained
p1: A contractual employee works for years, performs the same duties, and still may not get permanent status. Why? Because long service alone does not automatically create a right to regularisation.
p2: Many people believe that working continuously for an organisation means a contract employee must be made permanent. The reality is more complex. Courts often look at how the appointment happened, whether proper recruitment rules were followed, and if the position itself was created legally. A surprising point: even genuine long-term service may not be enough if the original appointment process did not meet required standards.
p3: Regularisation is not simply about rewarding years of work. It involves balancing employee expectations with legal rules on public recruitment, fairness, and equal opportunity. For organisations, clear contracts and transparent hiring processes matter. For employees, knowing their legal position before expecting permanent status can prevent confusion and disputes.
conclusion: Do you think long-serving contractual employees should get automatic permanent status, or should recruitment rules always come first?
